newsitem.title: UK: ICI 1st quarter profit slumps 68 pct.
newsitem.headline: ICI 1st quarter profit slumps 68 pct.

text.p: Britain's largest chemicals group ICI on Thursday reported a 68 percent plunge in first-quarter profits, which were hit by a strong pound and depressed prices.
ICI's shares dropped as the results were worse than expected and several analysts cut 1997 profit forecasts despite an upbeat company statement for the second half of the year.
Pre-tax profit before exceptional items fell to 65 million pounds ($106 million) from 202 million a year ago when bulk chemical prices peaked.
Prices started slumping shortly afterwards, but ICI said it saw them pick up again this quarter and consequently expected profits to improve in the second half of 1997.
"We are confident that prices will be firmer in the second quarter and that will affect our results," said finance director Alan Spall.
He highlighted the strong first quarter results of the paints business, where profits doubled, and emphasised "excellent" progress made in boosting productivity in the badly hit bulk chemicals.
But his soothing comments fell on deaf ears in the stock market where ICI shares fell 22 pence to 698-1/2 pence in late afternoon trade.
Kleinwort Benson analyst Jeremy Chantry said the poor result of industrial chemicals, which makes bulk products such as polyesters, was as expected.
But he was disappointed with ICI's materials sector, which suffered from price pressure in films and polyurethanes -- a plastic used in construction, furniture and automotive interiors.
The current pound strength was another reason for Chantry to cut his 1997 profit estimate by 100 million pounds to 490 million.
"The big two reasons for the downgrade are firstly the performance of the materials division and secondly the currency," Chantry said.
ICI said the strong pound could reduce full-year profit by about 120 million sterling if exchange rates remained at current levels.
The company had earlier indicated that competitive disadvantages stemming from the currency strength might shave 80 to 90 million pounds off 1997 profits.
But the hit may well be higher as the pound has gained further strength against the dollar and mark, Spall said.
He declined to comment on recent press reports saying ICI had tabled a bid for one of the chemicals units put up for sale by Unilever.
The operations offer high margins and are less volatile than the "heavy" industrial chemicals.
An acquisition of part of Unilever's chemicals operations would fit in well with ICI's stated strategy of moving more into "light" chemicals, analysts said.
But Spall merely repeated ICI's general strategy of focusing on "...value-creating acquisitions and organic growth in our strong leadership intermediate and surface coating business."
